root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward advancing, passing onward, and going beyond or past a limit.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development extends from a soul going forth and a thing passing away to an arrow overshooting its mark, an animal or person outstripping others, and related notions of depth, overflow, and excess. Some associated expressions have uncertain etymological relations.

senses.definition: To go forth or depart, especially of the soul; hence, to perish or die.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with the soul or selves. The lexical nuance includes going forth with difficulty; the Quran-focused explanation connects the soul’s departure with grief over something.

senses.definition: To pass away, come to nothing, or become null and ineffective.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a thing, especially falsehood, when it is overcome and made to pass away by truth.
An active participle describing something in the state or process of passing away.

senses.definition: Passing away, coming to nothing, or perishable.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression describing falsehood as a thing that passes away or comes to nothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an arrow, to pass beyond the butt or target and fall behind it; one report also uses it of going swiftly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use with an arrow; the report of swift movement is attached to the same expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To precede, outstrip, or go ahead of others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse, saddle-camel, or person who gets ahead of horses or horsemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bone, marrow, or a marrowy beast, to become compact and full of marrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence applies the description both to bones or marrow and to a beast characterized by exceptionally full marrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make falsehood pass away or come to nothing by means of truth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction in which truth is the agent and falsehood is made to disappear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a soul to depart; to slay.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative construction; killing is described as causing the soul to depart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause falsehood to pass away or come to nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of making what is false or vain disappear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an arrow pass beyond the butt or target.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with the arrow and its target.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shift a beast’s saddle forward and throw it onto its neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression concerning the movement of a saddle during travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move quickly in walking or journeying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of quick pace or travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a vessel; it is also reported with the meaning to overturn a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two interpretations are recorded as variant lexical explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast, to leap or move forward because of beating or fright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VII usage describing sudden movement under provocation or alarm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into a deep place, or from a mountain, and die.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction describing a fall ending in death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed part of the ground; a hollow or cavity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a depression in the ground, into which beasts may fall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, unsteady, or lightwitted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast, exceptionally fat or not exceeded in fatness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of an animal’s condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mare that precedes or outgoes the other horses or horsemen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a mare distinguished by speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression زُهَاقُ مِائَةٍ, numbering a hundred or being a group of one hundred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic numerical expression whose precise etymological relation to the root is uncertain in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep well; by extension, a place of destruction, a far-extending desert, or a pass of an overhanging mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A group of spatial applications associated with depth, danger, or difficult terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light or active.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use equivalent to being nimble or energetic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow passing beyond the butt and falling behind it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial description of an arrow’s course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Preceding, going ahead, or outstripping others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or saddle-camel that gets ahead of horses or horsemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man put to flight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of someone driven away or routed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water running vehemently; a canal running swiftly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of rapidly moving water or a channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast or its marrow: fat and marrow-rich, or, in contrary reports, very lean, dry, tough, or thin in marrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence explicitly records contrary physical descriptions rather than a single settled value; it applies the adjective both to beasts and to marrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mare with remarkable or swift running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun describing exceptional running qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression جَاءَتِ الخَيْلُ أَزَاهِقَ or أَزَاهِيقَ, horses or horsemen arriving in dispersed troops.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural idiom describing a group arriving in a scattered or dispersed formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of one whose soul has been caused to depart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slaying or a slayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description of the act or its agent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick in pace or journeying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative active-participial use for rapid travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loquacious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use recorded in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of the soul’s departure; figuratively, a camel that takes away the breath of other beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter use is an extended description of a camel so swift or exhausting that it deprives other riding animals of breath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Straitened or distressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person in a constrained condition.

cautions: The printed Classical citation attached to the expression إِنَّ البَاطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا uses an historical citation notation that does not match the independently supplied QAC location; the example is assigned to 17:81 only because QAC directly supplies that form and expression there.

The Classical descriptions of زَاهِق applied to beasts and marrow explicitly include contrary physical values, so they are kept separate from the Quranic perishing sense and are not reduced to one unqualified physical description.
